title: [YouPass Collect] - Employment rates of men and women aged 60-64 in four countries
prompt: The charts below show the percentages of men and women aged 60-64 in employment in four countries in 1970 and 2000. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar charts compare the employment rates of men and women aged between 60 and 64 in four different countries in 1970 and 2000.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while the proportion of employed elderly men declined dramatically in all four nations over the 30-year period, that of women showed little change. In addition, male employment figures were consistently higher than female ones in both years.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at male employment, Japan had the highest percentage in 1970 at 85%, followed by Belgium at 79%, while Australia and the USA recorded slightly lower figures of 76% and 73% respectively. By 2000, the most dramatic decline was seen in Belgium, where the proportion plummeted by 60 percentage points to just 19%. The fall was less severe but still significant in Australia, with a drop of 29 percentage points to 47%, while the USA saw a smaller decrease of 18 percentage points to 55%. Japan, despite experiencing the smallest decline of 11 percentage points, maintained the highest employment rate at 74% at the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for female employment, there were substantial variations between countries in 1970, with Japan having the highest rate at 43%, followed by the USA at 36%, while Australia and Belgium recorded much lower figures: 16% for the former and 8% for the latter. Both Japan and Belgium experienced decreases over the period, with Japan's figure falling by 3 percentage points to 40% and Belgium's declining marginally to 7%. In contrast, the rates in the USA and Australia showed slight increases, rising to 39% and 18% in that order by 2000.
